concepts.title: Keyboard Layout
concepts.summary: Locate white keys, black keys, and repeating octave patterns on the piano keyboard.

concepts.title: Finger Numbers
concepts.summary: Use the standard one-to-five numbering system to identify each finger of either hand.

concepts.title: Quarter-Note Rhythm
concepts.summary: Count and perform a steady pulse using quarter notes in common time.

concepts.title: Five-Finger Pattern
concepts.summary: Play five adjacent notes with a relaxed hand shape and consistent finger placement.

concepts.title: Stepwise Melody
concepts.summary: Read and perform a short melody that moves between adjacent notes.

concepts.title: Legato Phrasing
concepts.summary: Connect successive notes smoothly while keeping the pulse even.

concepts.title: Right-Hand Scale
concepts.summary: Coordinate a right-hand five-finger pattern across a one-octave scale.

concepts.title: Major Scale
concepts.summary: Recognize and perform the whole-step and half-step pattern of a major scale.

concepts.title: Basic Triad
concepts.summary: Build and identify a three-note major or minor chord in root position.

concepts.title: Simple Chord Progression
concepts.summary: Move between a small set of chords while maintaining a steady rhythm.
Perform an unfamiliar short exercise by combining note reading and pulse.

edges.rationale: Finger numbers are taught on the keyboard.
A five-finger pattern requires consistent finger identity.
The melody exercise requires a steady pulse.
The learner uses the five-finger position to play the melody.
Connected phrasing builds on controlled successive notes.
The scale starts with the same right-hand coordination.
The one-octave scale establishes the major-scale pattern.
Triads are introduced from scale degrees.
Chord changes require recognizable root-position triads.
Sight reading combines note recognition with a short melody.
Chord changes must remain inside a steady rhythm.
